newsitem.title: UK: World wool textile trade scents pick-up in orders.
newsitem.headline: World wool textile trade scents pick-up in orders.

text.p: Orders of woollen textiles in the major demand centres are beginning to pick up but competition for fresh business is intense, according to a new survey by the International Wool Secretariat (IWS).

The poll of 200 wool companies in Europe, Asia and Australia indicated better trading conditions in the tops and worsted yarn sectors during the final quarter of 1996 and mixed fortunes for fabric producers.
Respondents in Western Europe saw increased orders for tops and woollen fabric but orders of woollen yarn dropped off and stocks began to pile up.
Demand for worsted yarn remained steady against a background of burgeoning production and sales of woollen fabric were up.
Yarn orders are expected to improve in the first quarter of 1997 and yarn and top output is expected to run at higher levels than the opening quarter of 1996.
Strong demand and manageable stocks in the combing and weaving sectors kept the regional pick-up running.
Fourth-quarter tops production was up 43 percent on the previous year but the pace of growth is expected to ease to more sustainable levels by the end of March 1997.
Orders for worsted yarn were up but fabric orders were seen to slow, particularly in South Korea.
The IWS estimated Australian tops production at around twelve percent higher than fourth-quarter 1995 and order levels were also reported to be significantly greater.
The Australian mills surveyed expected production growth to slow in Q1 but output is estimated to be around six percent above 1996 levels.
They predicted tops demand would strengthen through to March.
The fourth-quarter of 1996 saw improved demand for machine-knitting yarn on the previous year but worsted weavers were overstocked as orders fell but output was unchanged.
The trade as a whole expected slower growth with worsted demand likely to remain steady. -London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
